newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money wedged in same range.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money wedged in same range.

text.p: * Volume narrows to 14.210 bln from 14.841 bln pesos
Manila overnight money was wedged at the same range of 10.5 to 10.46875 percent on Friday since most banks have already met their requirements for the week, traders said.
The average rate stood unchanged at 10.46875 percent, with 24 lenders and 18 borrowers.
In the secondary market of T-bills, trading was light but buying focus continued to be on short-term bills.
"It's better to go to the short tenors to be safe," a dealer said.

He said banks were awaiting developments on a possible hike in U.S. interest rates. When this happens, domestic interest rates may likewise rise to maintain the peso's premium over the U.S. dollar, he said.
According to a Reuter poll of five financial institutions, bid rates ranged from 10.50 to 10.55 percent for the three-month bills.
